name: Mercury (Hg)
summary: A toxic heavy metal. Organic methylmercury (from contaminated fish) targets the nervous system and crosses the placenta; inhaled elemental mercury vapour harms the lungs and brain; mercuric salts damage the kidneys.

conditions.label: Toxicity / exposure
conditions.description: Mercury binds sulphydryl groups and disrupts the nervous system, kidneys and, with vapour, the lungs.

affects.effect: Neurotoxicity — ataxia, tremor, paraesthesia, visual field loss
affects.detail: Methylmercury concentrates in the brain, causing sensory disturbance, ataxia, tremor, constricted visual fields and hearing loss (Minamata disease).

ageModifiers.infant: Prenatal methylmercury exposure disrupts neuronal migration, causing cerebral palsy-like syndromes and developmental delay.
ageModifiers.adult: Chronic vapour exposure causes tremor, erethism (irritability, shyness), insomnia and memory loss ('mad hatter').

genderModifiers.female: Methylmercury crosses the placenta and concentrates in the fetus; pregnant people are advised to limit high-mercury fish.

affects.detail: Inorganic mercuric salts accumulate in the proximal tubule, causing acute tubular necrosis or membranous nephropathy.
Acute inhalation of elemental mercury vapour causes cough, breathlessness and chemical pneumonitis.
Tingling around the mouth, hands and feet is an early sign of methylmercury toxicity.
